title: Limiting distance and fire-department response time
jurisdiction: British Columbia (specific local authority not named in published decision)

facts.text: A six-unit residential townhouse complex has no dwelling unit above another, is non-sprinklered, and was designed under Part 9. It is within 500 m by roadway of the responding fire hall.
The local fire service said it could not ensure a response within ten minutes for at least 90% of late-night calls; the appellant argued proximity should control.
The cited rule adjusts limiting distance where response time exceeds ten minutes in at least 10% of calls and a storey is not sprinklered.
